title: Airflow: DAGs, tasks, operators and the execution date

videos.script: Ana's nightly script works. What it lacks is everything around it. {{around}} Something to start it at two in the morning. To run its steps in order. To try again when one fails, and to remember which nights worked. {{needs}} Airflow is that something. It does not move data. It runs the programs that do. {{airflow}} Ana writes her steps as a DAG: six tasks, and the arrows between them. {{dag}} Her first test run fails, in the middle of a hundred and thirty-four lines of log. One space fixes it. {{fail}} Then the run for the third of March loads the second. Today, and next year, and whenever it is run again. {{date}} Because a task that asks the run which day it is for, instead of asking the clock, can always do the same work twice.
